gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: I'd rather she ___ the accounts this month, to be honest.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather + subject' takes the past form for an unreal present preference.
avoid is followed by -ing: avoid talking.

gaps.sentence: The box was heavy enough ___ two people.
gaps.explanation: adjective + enough + to-infinitive: heavy enough to need.

gaps.sentence: She keeps ___ about the exam results.
It was kind of them ___ us a lift to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'It was kind of them to give …' — to-infinitive after the adjective.

gaps.sentence: I've always wanted ___ how to sail.
The teacher made us ___ the whole essay again.
gaps.explanation: 'Make someone do' — active 'make' takes the bare infinitive.
